_meta.indication: APHEXDA, a hematopoietic stem cell mobilizer, is indicated in combination with filgrastim (G-CSF) to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells to the peripheral blood for collection and subsequent autologous transplantation in patients with multiple myeloma.

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to motixafortide 1.25 mg/kg with G-CSF or placebo with G-CSF for HSC mobilization.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ages 18-78 years with multiple myeloma undergoing HSC mobilization for autologous transplantation.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: proportion of subjects that mobilized ≥6 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg in up to 2 apheresis sessions.
pivotal_trials.result: Responders 67.5% (motixafortide) vs 9.5% (placebo); CMH common proportions difference 56.8% (95% CI 42.6-71%; p<0.0001); odds ratio 15.1 (95% CI 4.86-46.9).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >20%): injection site reactions (73%), injection site pain (53%), pruritus (38%), flushing (33%), injection site erythema (27%), injection site pruritus (24%), back pain (21%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 5.4% of patients; anaphylactic shock occurred in 0.7% of treated patients (n=407).
target_moa: Motixafortide is a selective antagonist/inhibitor of the C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4 (CXCR4) that blocks binding of its ligand SDF-1α/CXCL12; CXCR4-SDF-1α signaling is involved in the trafficking and homing of hematopoietic stem cells to the marrow, and blockade mobilizes HSCs to peripheral blood.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because this is not the first drug for this specific indication or first-in-pharmacological class and it did not raise significant public health questions.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation (#12-3719) granted July 6, 2012 for motixafortide for use in combination with G-CSF to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells from the marrow to peripheral blood for collection for autologous or allogeneic transplantation.

citations.quote: In 2012, motixafortide was granted orphan drug designation for use in combination with G-CSF to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) from the marrow to peripheral blood for collection for autologous or allogeneic transplantation.

Orphan drug designation (#12-3719) for motixafortide for use in the mobilization of hematopoietic stem cells from the marrow to the peripheral blood for collection for autologous or allogeneic transplantation was granted on July 6, 2012.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) review of NDA 217159, received September 9, 2022, approved based on the single adequate and well-controlled GENESIS trial plus confirmatory evidence; motixafortide held FDA orphan drug designation. It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.
